I don’t think I wrapped my head around just how much $ANT is going to be spending on training.

Market rightfully reacted when learning how little ANT was spending on serving customers vs. training with their ~25% split. The implication when you roll fwd Compute / % going to training is pretty eye opening.

My ANT base case is they spend ~6x more on training/RL models by end of ‘27 vs. the current / Opus 5.5 class model. When you factor in efficiency gains (esp on the RL side), it is probably closer to a 10x increase in effective training. I personally can’t fathom what that leads to.

What does it mean for ANT (and not too too far behind OAI) to spend 10x more effective compute training models over the next year?

The Cape detour added two to three weeks a voyage and absorbed 5 to 7 per cent of global container capacity. That capacity is coming back just as the fleet grows 9 per cent in 2027 and the orderbook sits at 45 per cent of existing ships. 

Shanghai to Rotterdam freight is already down 29 per cent from its July peak.

None of this shows up in a New Keynesian model, where growth is inflationary and every strong number demands another hike. The Fed has it backw

Memory: Goldman has DRAM short 4.1 per cent in 2026, 5.1 per cent in 2027 and 1.2 per cent in 2028. The 2027 gap is the widest in 15+ years. Demand beats supply every year.

Suppliers: Samsung’s 2027 HBM is sold out. SK hynix sees demand above supply through 2030. Micron has “no line of sight” to balance. New fabs arrive in 2028 and later.

Wafers: HBM rises to nearly 30 per cent of DRAM wafer input in 2027 and takes 3 to 4x the wafers per bit. 

Conventional DRAM gets squeezed.
CPUs: NVDA says agentic AI demand for CPUs is “far outstripping supply” and sees CPU revenue more than doubling.

GPUs: a three-year-old H100 rents for $ 3.07 an hour, up 54 per cent in a year. CoreWeave has 10x more demand than capacity through 2027, and 2028 is already several times capacity.

Capex: cloud spending is up another 60 per cent in 2027, to about $ 1.5 trillion.

If demand were fading, old chips would get cheaper. They are getting dearer.

AI demand is strong. Ignore the doomers.

The memory upcycle in two charts:

DRAM:
• Contract prices started climbing in 3Q25 and were up ~45% QoQ by 4Q25
• 1Q26 was the peak: blended ASP roughly doubled in one quarter, with PC DDR5 up ~110%
• 2Q26 added another ~60%, led by server DDR4 at ~70%

NAND:
• Later and a bit smaller: ~+30% in 4Q25, ~+57% in 1Q26, ~+75% in 2Q26
• Enterprise SSD led both quarters at ~+80%

What's forecast next:
• 3Q26: DRAM ~+15%, NAND ~+20%
• 4Q26: both around +10%
• 2027: DRAM flattens to low single digits, while NAND turns negative from 2Q27 and is falling 10–15% QoQ by 4Q27

Prices are still rising, but the rate of change peaked in 1H26. And the forecasts say NAND rolls over well before DRAM does.

text:
HACKERS BREACH U.S. AIR FORCE'S FLAGSHIP CLOUD PLATFORM 

Hackers have breached Cloud One, one of the U.S. military's largest cloud computing platforms, according to Reuters, citing three people familiar with the matter.

The platform supports sensitive military operations, personnel records, logistics and weapons tracking, using infrastructure from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet.

U.S. Cyber Command has reportedly been called in to assess the damage, while application migrations and security updates have been disrupted.

One source said attackers exploited a software vulnerability to access the platform's control plane.

The hackers' identity, the full extent of the breach and whether sensitive data was stolen remain unknown.

The Air Force declined to comment on the security status of specific system

- The company is currently not supplying Eoptolink because its own CW laser capacity is insufficient to meet its demand. (positive for merchant laser players)

Their primary suppliers include Tongmei (AXT subsidary), Xiandao and Yunnan Germanium.

Also bullish signal regarding market capture for other merchant laser players. 

- The average delivery lead time for MOCVD equipment remains stable at approximately 12 months. ($AIXA and related unchanged). 

- CW laser products were 80% of the company's total revenue: (60% 70mW, 33–34% 100mW, rest misc). 

- "At present, DSP supply shortages have not been incorporated as a core variable in detailed calculations."

$AAOI is not alone here

text:
Now let’s use facts. 

•  Nvidia’s Singapore subsidiary booked roughly $104 billion in revenue in 2025 (and ~$118 billion over the 12 months to January 2026). That is a large figure, but Singapore functions heavily as a billing/invoicing hub. Nvidia has previously stated that actual shipments to Singapore itself were under 2% of total revenue; most products billed there are shipped elsewhere (including some Taiwan and China business routed through the subsidiary).
•  Under Nvidia’s current geographic reporting (by customer headquarters rather than billing location), the United States accounts for roughly 69% of FY2026 revenue (~$216 billion total), Taiwan ~20%, China (incl. Hong Kong) ~9%, and “Other” ~2%. There is no standalone Singapore line that equates to half the business.
•  The restrictions apply to advanced chips destined for those specific countries (with exemptions), not to Nvidia’s global sales. The company has stated that demand continues to far exceed supply and that it expects performance to remain strong while it assesses the new rules.

Alice Huang does not appear to be a spy for China... 

but she is a hustler working for a company funded by Alibaba, which wanted GPUs... 

in defiance of intended US export control...

and also in defiance of Chinese government directives to use domestic chips and stop using Nvidia chips, yeah?  

Wherein the actions were not technically illegal under US or Chinese law, but went against the known wishes of both governments?

And now we find that Alibaba and most Chinese AI labs other than Deepseek have mostly built their models on distillation of US labs and now that Anthropic has put a stop to it (apparently poisoning the data), the latest Chinese model releases are DOA?

A truly indigenous Chinese model pre-trained on real-world human data would be more possible in China (it costs money but would be cheaper than anything US labs could get) and would yield a materially superior model with data not available to US frontier labs - and would give the world an badly-needed AI voice based on a culture distinct from the West.

So what actually happened here is that Alice Huang harmed *China* by facilitating Chinese AI lab dependence on US chips, and also caused the US to trip up a bit by getting Jensen fired for a week and creating yet another tiresome political fault line.

zh_summary: Does a $VIX spike mean buy? Discusses academic evidence, rebuttals and conclusion on whether expected equity returns step up after fear gauge spikes.
en_summary: Does a $VIX spike mean buy? Discusses academic evidence, rebuttals and conclusion on whether expected equity returns step up after fear gauge spikes.
text:
https://www.atlaspeakresearch.com/backtests/peak-vix/

DOES A $VIX SPIKE MEAN BUY? THE ACADEMIC EVIDENCE, THE REBUTTALS, AND A CONCLUSION

THE CLAIM

The folk version says buy when the fear gauge screams. The academic version is narrower and more interesting: expected equity returns step up, nonlinearly, after implied volatility reaches extreme levels, and the step-up is large enough to measure years of data at a time. Both versions circulate every time the VIX prints 30 or 35. They are not the same claim, and the literature supports them very differently.

THE EVIDENCE FOR

• Ronn and Xu (Econometrics, 2025) test the folk version directly. Across 29 historical episodes in which the VIX exceeded 30, a strategy of cutting equity exposure above 30 and buying back when volatility subsided underperformed simply holding through the episodes by 10.9% a year. Subsequent S&P 500 returns rose with the level of the VIX. Their conclusion for investors with a high appetite for risk: when the VIX is high, invest, because on average you will be compensated.

• Bansal and Stivers (Financial Management, 2025), over 1990 to 2023, find the equity premium steps up appreciably when the VIX exceeds a threshold around its 80th to 85th percentile, with predictive adjusted R-squared of about 19% at six months and 29% at twelve months, robust across subperiods and out of sample. The relationship is a step, not a slope: below the threshold there is little to harvest, above it the premium jumps.

• Ban

Up to 400MW.

$15B+.

Targeted around 2028.
